title: Rescue Teams Go
description: International rescue teams deploy forward from Misawa Air Base to assist the victims of Japan's earthquake and tsunami. Produced by Senior Airman Barbara Patton. jpearthquake11

transcript.text: Watch to help with the search for Mesquite in the disaster area.
We've been tasked hopefully to work with the two teams from the United States as a joint team
and see if we can provide some assistance in search for Mesquite.
We haven't actually been given a mission directly but I think it's about 125km
further south from where we are at the moment.
I'm not sure the name of the town.
But when we get there we're travelling by convoy to get there.
To provide search for Mesquite, hopefully jointly we'll be working together with the Americans
and that way we can provide search and rescue to any of the collapse buildings that we find.
And if the areas have been fully searched we'll be providing some research into the areas of body recovery.
Well yeah obviously we're hoping there's not going to be too much devastation but we've been told
that the tsunami came in at least a kilometer into the town that we're heading to.
And we're just hoping that there's not too much devastation there.
And we can provide as much assistance as possible really.
I think it's been working really well at the moment.
There's a lot of political issues and a lot of logistics to get ready,
especially with mobilising all the equipment.
But that's been going smoothly.
There's always a few problems along the way that slow us up.
And obviously everyone would like to be out there sooner.
But at the moment I think it's been going well.
Just to let everyone know that we are here we're keen to get out and help as much as we can.
And thanks to the support, especially from the American base here,
and the support that everyone's given us so far.
Right now we're getting ready to send out a convoy down south.
We're going to a town just north of Sendai.
Approximately seven tractor trailers worth of equipment.
And approximately five to six buses worth of people and equipment as well are getting ready to head out.
It's going to be quite a donning task.
We're looking about six hours worth of drive time to head down there
to get some relief to these people that are been hit by the tsunami and the earthquake.
Right now the goal is to get the relief workers that you see around the building here
to the people who need it most, to get the working dogs so they can start helping
find people that are still buried even three days after the earthquake.
We're going to unload the equipment by hand.
That's going to be a daunting task in itself.
And then basically we're going to turn and burn and come right on back and pick up the next batch.
We're going two drivers per vehicle, one sleeps, one drives,
and it's probably going to be a 24 hour shift for most of us
until we get the people down there who needs to be down there.
Right now there's all sorts of different nationalities here, different countries
that are participating in this operation.
We have the British. I've seen some of the Japanese here.
I've seen some of the British here, the US here.
I've seen some of the California, LA firefighters, that sort of thing.
They're out here as well. So we've got quite a diverse group of people here helping in this operation.
Right now for this goal is more or less just getting the people and the equipment down to where it's needed.
In terms of long term that may be happening, but right now our goal is just to get stuff and people down there.
Even three days after the quake and the tsunami, people are without power, without help and without water and food.
So that's what we're just trying to get something down there going.
